focus: Test the remaining Claude adapters against the three fork transcripts and look for a platform-level fork-scoped event
keyFindings: The platform fires a dedicated `SubagentStart` event whose matcher is `fork` inside sub-agents — 3, 8 and 6 occurrences in the 14:44, 15:30 and 17:42 forks — so fork-ness is observable at the platform level even though the SessionStart payload itself carries no fork field.
The project's SessionStart adapters do run inside forks: session-prime, worktree-guard, check-git-hooks, git-live-follow and compact-pointer all produced hook_success entries in the fork transcripts.

The project's PostToolUse `context-nudge` and Stop `stop-arm` adapters produced no attachment at all in any of the three forks; the only PostToolUse entries were the Orca agent-hook bridge, so the fork hazard is confined to SessionStart dispatch plus whatever the injected seed makes the model do.

Every hook attachment inside a fork carries `agentId` and `isSidechain: true` on the transcript record itself, so the fork's identity is provable from the transcript while it is absent from the payload the adapter receives.

`worktree-guard` announced "This top-level session is running on the shared 'main' checkout" inside a fork, a second adapter that assumes it is addressing a top-level session — evidence the assumption is family-wide rather than one hook's bug.

`context-nudge` needs only `session_id` and `transcript_path` and writes state under the payload session id exactly as compact-pointer does, so if PostToolUse dispatch ever reaches forks the same parent-state overwrite appears there too.
